questions.stem: Which of the following is a non-renewable energy resource?

options.text: Solar power
Wind power
Natural gas
Hydroelectric power

questions.explanation: Natural gas is a non-renewable (finite) energy resource because it takes millions of years to form from the remains of ancient organisms. Once used up, it cannot be replaced on a human timescale.

questions.stem: What is the main advantage of renewable energy sources over fossil fuels?

options.text: They always produce more energy
They will not run out and generally produce fewer greenhouse gas emissions during use
They are always cheaper
They work in all weather conditions

questions.explanation: Renewable energy sources like wind, solar, and hydroelectric will not run out and produce little or no carbon dioxide during electricity generation, unlike fossil fuels which release CO2 and will eventually be exhausted.

options.text: A fuel made from ancient fossils
A fuel produced from recently living biological materials, such as plants or animal waste
A fuel made from nuclear reactions
A fuel that only works in biology laboratories

questions.explanation: Biofuels are made from recently living biological materials. Examples include biodiesel (from plant oils), bioethanol (from fermenting sugars), and biogas (from decomposing waste). They are considered renewable.

questions.stem: Why are biofuels sometimes described as 'carbon neutral'?

options.text: Because they contain no carbon
Because the CO2 released when they burn was recently absorbed by the plants during photosynthesis
Because they produce no gases when burned
Because they are mixed with water before use

questions.explanation: Biofuels are considered carbon neutral because the carbon dioxide released during combustion was absorbed from the atmosphere by the plants during their growth. However, energy used in production and transport means they are not truly carbon neutral in practice.

questions.stem: What is a disadvantage of using wind turbines for energy?

options.text: They produce large amounts of carbon dioxide
They are intermittent -- they only generate electricity when the wind is blowing
They use fossil fuels to operate
They cause acid rain

questions.explanation: Wind turbines are intermittent because they only generate electricity when the wind blows. This means they cannot provide a constant, reliable supply of electricity and need backup from other energy sources or energy storage.

questions.stem: What environmental problem is associated with burning fossil fuels for energy?

options.text: It produces too much oxygen
It releases carbon dioxide (contributing to climate change) and other pollutants like sulfur dioxide
It uses too much water
It causes earthquakes

questions.explanation: Burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide (a greenhouse gas contributing to climate change), sulfur dioxide (causing acid rain), nitrogen oxides, particulates, and carbon monoxide, all of which harm the environment and human health.

questions.stem: Why is hydrogen considered a potential clean fuel for the future?

options.text: Because it is the most abundant element on Earth's surface
Because when hydrogen burns, the only product is water, with no carbon dioxide emissions
Because it is easy to store and transport
Because it is cheaper than all other fuels

questions.explanation: When hydrogen burns, the only product is water (2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O), so no carbon dioxide or other pollutants are produced. However, challenges remain around producing hydrogen cleanly and storing it safely.
